title.narrative: Policy Coherence for Adaptation and Resilience

description.narrative: Contract related to: Policy Coherence for Adaptation and Resilience - The action addresses two interlinked priority areas. The overall objective is to support fragile and crisis-affected regions, countries and communities to achieve resilience and sustain peace by addressing the climate and environmental risks that drive conflict and instability, through two components focusing on interrelated priorities :1.     Equip partners with tools to better align crisis and conflict prevention frameworks and climate adaptation policies;2.     Support communities and authorities in fragile contexts to better address risks to their security related to increased demand for extractive materials in fragile contexts.Component 1: Conflict Sensitive National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) and climate-sensitive preventive mechanisms/early-warning systems (EUR 2 m)National Adaptation Plans are one of the main implementation tools of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climae Change (UNFCCC), however they have varying success in ensuring that the adaptation actions contained within take sufficient care to mitigate risks to peace and security. Support to integrated policy development and coordination to ensure policy coherence would thus be beneficial to partner countries which have an identified need for support in this area.Conversely, engagement in states vulnerable to conflict may not always take account of the latent and emerging climate and environment-related risks in conflict prevention frameworks. Ensuring that adaptation strategies and processes are conflict sensitive and that climate and environment-related threats to security are fully understood are integral to a effective response to these multifaceted challenges.for. Component 2: Critical Raw materials/extractives risk-mitigation (EUR 4 m)The European Green Deal and its Industrial Plan foresee a transformation to a net-zero economy which depends on extraction of raw materials which are frequently located in fragile contexts. This transition can have wide-ranging effects on security and social cohesion of communities in such contexts. or relative institutional strength. Support to community engagement and capacity development as well as dialogue with law enforcement will contribute to mitigation of security risks related to extraction of Critical Raw Materials.In addressing the interdependence between security and climate change, the both components action directly responds to one objective of the Thematic Programme for Peace, Stability and Conflict prevention which aims to strengthen capacities, institutions and policies and support relevant initiatives at local national, regional and multinational levels to understand and address climate security risks. It also presents linkages with another specific objective of the thematic MIP, namely to: `Support initiatives addressing the conflict dynamics related to climate change and environmental degradation and sustainable management of natural resources¿.The action responds to research and analysis from external partners and has been developed to complement ongoing actions addressing the climate-security nexus and to reflect policy developments and legislative proposals, including the Joint Communication on the Climate-Security Nexus as well as the external dimension of the Green Deal, notably the Critical Raw Materials
